register.description: Antenna Diversity State Machine (BB_ANT_DIVS) (0x4bb1) In partial diversity, the antennas switch based on the dwell time. When barkerSync is valid at the end of a dwell time, the current antenna is declared as the one to use for the incoming packet. If the packet is later lost (or after it is completely received), the antenna switching (and searching for a new packet) will start again. In b-only full diversity, the antennas will switch based on dwell time until barkerSync is valid at the end of a dwell time. At that point the current antenna is declared the first antenna and the full diversity algorithm starts. The other full diversity modes are 11g compatible and do not switch antennas until after the rxtb block is granted control of the packet with the rxt_go_b signal. They allow control of the starting antenna when using full diversity - antenna 1 as we had in the past, and now new options to start on antenna 2 or the last antenna a packet was received on. bitfield.description: Dwell_TimeDefines the antenna dwell time in micro seconds. This is the amount of time the TNETW1150 remains on an antenna when switching between antennas in one of the diversity modes. A dwell time of 0xA has been determined to be optimal for the TNETW1150. 00000 is a special case and will be interpreted as 00001.

Ant_Diversity (802.11b-only mode, in which antennas are switched until an 11b acknowledgement. Set 0x2002 to 0x2 for 11b-only processing.) (802.11b-only mode, in which antennas are switched until an 11b acknowledgement. The last antenna selected is then used as the starting antenna for full diversity. Set 0x2002 to 0x2 for 11b-only processing.)Note: For full diversity modes, registers 0x4BD4, 0x4BD5, 0x4BD6, and 0x2003 must also be programmed.Note: Antenna1 and antenna2 refer to the RXANT0 and RXANT1 fields in register BB_ANT_SEL_CFG, respectively, which specify the actual mapping of radio control signals for antenna selection. 0x0: Antenna 1 fixed (never switch to antenna 2) (default) 0x1: Antenna 2 fixed (never switch to antenna 1) 0x2: Full Diversity, Antenna1-Start Mode 0x3: Partial Diversity 0x4: Full Diversity, Antenna2-Start Mode 0x5: Full Diversity, Last-RX-Antenna-Start Mode 0x6: Full Diversity, 802.11b-Only Mode

register.description: This register specifies the supported modulation modes for 11b. The default specifies all available modulation modes. Specific modes are disabled by writing a "0" to the corresponding bit. If a packet is received with a modulation type that is disabled, it will be discarded, and RX_STAT[3] will be set to indicate an unsupported modulation error.

bitfield.description: De-scrambler DisableSetting this bit disables the internal de-scrambler. When this bit is cleared (default), the de-scrambler is enabled.

0 - The 11b receiver is ready to receive DSSS and CCK packets (1,2,5.5,11 Mbps). (Default) 1 - The 11b receiver is ready to receive only DSSS packets (1,2 Mbps). This setting saves power by disabling the FFE and DFE adaptation during the 11b preamble. CCK packets will be classifed as unsupported by the PLCP.
when asserted this bit enables the crc 1-bit correction mechanism.

This bit controls the CCK (HighRate) power saving mode. Power is reduced by turning the bulkDelay module on only when an 11b packet is detected. This reduces quiescent listen current by approximately 100uA. The bulkDelay clock is called hrbdClk80, and hrbdClk80_en controls it. 0 - The power reduction is active (Default). This setting introduces very small (and unnoticeable) performance degradation, due to the small reduction in FFE and DFE adaptation time. 1 - The power reduction is not active. bulkDelay is active all the time. This setting better resembles the 1271 and 1251.

This bit controls an RTL change that was made, which reduces the 11b Rx-listen current by ~350uA. The RTL change is not supposed to have any implication on performance. This bit stops the HRDemod_inputs_en from blocking the slot[2:0] signal to all the High-Rate modules. 0 - The power saving change is active (Default) 1 - No power savings. This mode better resembles the 1251 and 1273.

FFE_Enable Setting this bit enables the FFE during the payload portion of a packet. The FFE is always enabled (when the high rate demod is enabled) before the payload. The default is disabled during the payload.
DFE Time Constant This Field contains the DFE time constant. Should write with the default value 0b01.
DFE Number of Taps - Specifies the number of DFE Taps to use. 00 - Zero taps (DFE disabled) 01 - 2 taps 10 - 4 taps 11 - 8 taps

Bypass DFE - When unset, DFE coefficients and FFE output are fed to the decoder. When set, zeros are fed to the decoder instead of the DFE coefficients, and the slicer inputs (FFE output + DFE output) are fed to the decoder instead of the FFE output.

register.description: This register is used to balance the delay paths from the low rate block to the high rate block. It should not be modified during normal operation. NOTE: Software that previously wrote to this register will cause problems. This register only used 3 bits before and that value was added to 0d28 to calculate the final offset. Now the full 6-bit offset needs to be written. NOTE1: Because of the design changes from Legolas to this RTL, this register has to be written a value which is three more than what it was for Legolas. For Example if a value of 6'h20 was being programmed for Legolas then for this RTL we need to program 6'h23.

register.description: This read-only register indicates the estimated noise power of the equalized receive signal at the input of the FEC decoder. The noise measurement becomes valid at the end of the PLCP header.
This read-only register indicates the multipath power level, which is an estimated value proportional to the signal-to-ISI ratio observed on the received signal.

bitfield.description: High-Rate PLL Bandwidth 0000 - 228 kHz 0101 - 113 kHz 1010 - 56 kHz 1111 - 28 kHz (default)
Barker PLL Bandwidth 0000 - 201 kHz 0101 - 66 kHz 1010 - 30 kHz 1111 - 15 kHz (default)
PLL Initialization Configuration - This field specifies the number of samples used by the PLL initialization module. The value of this field is an unsigned integer from 0 to 15.

Barker Detect Time Constant. This field contains the Barker correlator detect time constant. It is recommended that you use the default value, 0b1110, when writing to this field. This field controls an accumulator that keeps a running power estimate. The individual bits for the feedback are explained below: 3 - Add 1/2 of old accum to new correlator power 2 - Add 1/4 of old accum to new correlator power 1 - Add 1/8 of old accum to new correlator power 0 - Add 1/16 of old accum to new correlator power

AGC Hold Delay. This field indicates the number of Barker symbols for which the analog AGC remains in short integration mode after the correlator obtains Barker Sync. See Section 3.6 AGC Notes on page 29 for more information on how the AGCs are controlled.
Barker Miss Threshold. This field specifies the number of missed correlations before the Barker correlators drops synchronization.
Barker Match Threshold. This field specifies the number of matched correlations needed for the Barker correlator to establish synchronization.
False Lock Threshold. This field contains the false lock threshold. It is recommended that you use the default value, 0x8, when writing to this field.
Barker Miss in Search. This field specifies the number of missed correlations during Barker synchronization before the state machine is reset.

register.description: This register contains the Barker correlator output threshold, which determines when to start the Barker synchronization state machine. BKR_THRESH1(0x4bdb) is a closely related register. Any change to BKR_THRESH register value would also require a change to BKR_THRESH1 register.

11 Mbit/s Update Period. This field specifies the FFE update period for 11 Mbit/s packets as shown below: 000: Constant update 001: 2 symbols 010: 4 symbols 011: 6 symbols (default) 100: 8 symbols 101: 10 symbols 110: 12 symbols 111: 14 symbols

bitfield.description: Number of barker symbols to use for for the digital AGC long integration mode. After analog AGC freeze, this field sets the amount of time to allow for individual long integration periods of the digital AGC. When this time elapses, the digital AGC freezes for the rest of the packet.

Number of barker symbols to use for the analog AGC long integration mode. After barker sync (11b packet detection), this field sets the amount of time to allow for individual long integration periods of the analog AGC. When this time elapses, the analog AGC freezes and the digital AGC begins operation with long integration periods.

register.description: This register contains the result of 11b EVM block. The value is in Two's complement and in decibel scale. The algorithm is different for low rate and high rate receivers in 11b so EVM of a low rate packet cannot be compared with EVM of a high rate packet. This register is updated at the end of a received packet. This register is also listed under the "EVM IP Block"/cgt.

register.description: The register corresponding to BKR_THRESH >>1. Now this need not be BKR_THRESH >>1. In fact the default value is same as BKR_THRESH. This change was made due to the change in agc behavior. This register was added for 1150/1251. To make the algorithm equivalent to that of 1140 program half the value that is being programmed to BKR_THRESH register 0x4BCF.

bitfield.description: If the number of saturations of analog 80 Mhz ADC (either I or Q) is more than adc_sat_thresh in a block of 40 samples (0.5us), the barker state machine and the 22 correlator power accumulators are reset. This is done only if bit 6 is high and the current Barker state is SEARCH or PRE_SYNC.
Enable the option to reset the Barker State and correlators. By default this is disabled.

When this bit is set the signal 'rxtb_cca' going out of rxtb module is gated with rxt_go_b signal coming from g state machine. That means when rxt_go_b is low, rxtb_cca always indicates clear channel.

If the number of saturations of 22Mhz 11b Digital AGC outputs (either I or Q) is more than digagc_sat_thresh in a block of 11 samples (0.5us), the barker state machine and the 22 correlator power accumulators are reset. This is done only if bit 4 is high and the current Barker state is SEARCH or PRE_SYNC.
Enable the option to reset the Barker State and correlators. By default this is disabled.

The dwell time in microseconds when antenna is in Check First. Programming this register with the same value as 0x4BB1[4:0] will make it backward compatible with Legolas PG1.1. When antenna diversity is FULL (i.e. 0x4BB1[7:5]=010) we don t have to dwell in first antenna for more than say 3-4 us after barker sync. So the preferred value of this is 0x04 when diversity is FULL. Otherwise this should be same as 0x4BB1[4:0]. MatanY - TODO - Can be removed?

AGC_HOLD_DLY2. This field indicates the number of Barker symbols for which the analog AGC remains in short integration mode after the correlator obtains Barker Sync in antennas Check Second and Check Third. This Register is provided because the agc is already in short integration till barker Sync is obtained and since the barker detect delay is typically 7-8 us this extra dwelling need not be there. Programming this to zero will make the agc go from Short to Long Integration just after getting the Barker Sync. Programming AGC_HOLD_DLY2 to the same value as 0x4BCC[7:4] will make it backward compatible with Legolas PG1.1.The recommended value of AGC_HOLD_DLY2 is 0x0.
